Veena, in Kannur and Thiruvananthapuram, alleging that her defunct firm received substantial monthly retainers from **Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL)** between 2017 and 2021 without rendering any tangible service. The raids triggered protests across the state, with CPI(M) activists allegedly vandalizing vehicles carrying ED officials.  The ED is verifying bank transactions of Ms. Veena while stating no incriminating documents were found at Mr. Vijayan's residence.

recent_articles.title: ED freezes ₹18.36 crore and 242 bank accounts Exalogic-CMRL payoff case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **ED** froze ₹18.36 crore in 242 accounts following raids conducted on Wednesday as part of an alleged pay-off case involving **T. Veena**, daughter of Kerala's Leader of the Opposition, **Pinarayi Vijayan**. The searches targeted premises linked to Ms. Veena and the management of the **CMRL** (Kannur Metro Rail Limited) in Kerala and Bengaluru.  The ED is investigating proceeds of crime generated by the CMRL, led by S.N. Sasidharan Kartha, along with Ms. Veena. The investigation stems from previous findings by the Income Tax department that revealed fake expenses amounting to ₹130 crore.

recent_articles.title: Report ‘phone hack’ to police or I will do it for you, Labour chair tells Farage | Nigel Farage | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nigel Farage** has been given 24 hours by **Anna Turley**, the **Labour** party chair, to report to security services whether his phone was hacked by Russia-linked actors or the party will do it for him.  The incident, which involves a £5 million gift from cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne, has sparked skepticism and calls for independent investigation. **Ciaran Martin**, former head of the National Cyber Security Centre, called Farage's claims "unsubstantiated" and urged him to report the matter to authorities. The parliamentary commissioner for standards is also investigating whether Farage broke any rules by not declaring the gift.

recent_articles.title: Probe incidents of accused being paraded in underwear: APDR writes to West Bengal Human Rights Commission - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A civil rights organization, the **Association of Protection of Democratic Rights (APDR)**, has filed a complaint with the **West Bengal Human Rights Commission** alleging that police officers in Howrah district paraded two accused individuals in their underwear and vests. The APDR cites two incidents at Golabari and Sankrail police stations on May 24th and 25th respectively, where the accused were subjected to this treatment.  The organization argues that these actions violate human rights and are a form of "criminal force" by law enforcement.

recent_articles.title: Spain police enter PM Sanchez’s Socialist Party HQ in corruption probe | Politics News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Spanish** police entered the headquarters of the **Socialist Workers’ Party (PSOE)** in Madrid as part of an investigation into possible financial wrongdoing. The search is focused on former party member Leire Diez and follows audio recordings that suggested her involvement in attempts to discredit a Civil Guard anticorruption unit member.  The **National Court** judge Santiago Pedraz is leading the inquiry, while the head of the main opposition **People’s Party (PP), Alberto Nunez Feijoo**, has called for early elections due to allegations of corruption within the government.

recent_articles.title: Revealed: Mandelson vetting warned of ties to senior figures in China, Russia and Israel | Peter Mandelson | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Peter Mandelson** was denied security clearance by the UK's vetting agency, **United Kingdom Security Vetting (UKSV)**, due to concerns about his relationships with senior figures in China, Russia and Israel. These included ties to Lan Fo’an, a Chinese finance minister; Oleg Deripaska, a Russian oligarch; and Tamir Hayman, a former Israeli military intelligence general. UKSV flagged these connections as areas of concern and noted Mandelson's relationship with Deripaska, despite sanctions imposed on him by the EU and UK. The agency also expressed concerns about a £1 million loan Mandelson received to invest in an Israeli startup and his past associations with Jeffrey Epstein. Despite this, **Olly Robbins**, the then Foreign Office permanent secretary, granted Mandelson security clearance anyway.  The government is now facing scrutiny over its handling of the vetting process and whether it has complied fully with parliamentary demands for transparency.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool MLA arrested, several leaders quit party post - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dilip Mondal**, a Trinamool Congress MLA from Bishnupur, was arrested by **West Bengal police** in Odisha on Wednesday (May 27, 2026) after days of evading arrest. The arrest follows an investigation into alleged threats against **BJP** workers during the West Bengal Assembly elections and a previous complaint filed against him.  The arrest marks the first time a sitting MLA has been apprehended by **West Bengal police**. This comes amidst a wave of arrests targeting local Trinamool Congress workers, including former Minister **Sujit Bose**, for their alleged involvement in corruption and post-poll violence. The situation is further complicated by mass resignations from Trinamool leaders, including senior leader **Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar** and several councillors.  The party's leadership is also facing criticism for the lack of a designated space for the Leader of Opposition, **Sovandeb Chattopadhyay**, in the West Bengal Assembly premises.

recent_articles.title: Balen Shah's two-month report card: Why Nepal’s Gen Z hero is under fire already - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah, known as Balen, is facing scrutiny over the pace of his ambitious reform agenda.  The government tracker shows many promises are behind schedule and there have been resignations within his cabinet. Concerns about his governing style, including ordinances bypassing parliament and controversial eviction drives, have also emerged. While he campaigned on transparency and accountability, Balen has not addressed the nation or held a press conference in two months. Protests have erupted over stricter customs enforcement at the Indo-Nepal border, impacting trade between India and Nepal.

recent_articles.title: Defiant Pinarayi Vijayan raises fist after ED raid, vows ‘long battle’ against BJP and Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pinarayi Vijayan**, former Kerala Chief Minister and now Leader of the Opposition, emerged from his residence in Thiruvananthapuram to greet hundreds of **CPI(M)** workers protesting against a seven-hour raid by the **Enforcement Directorate (ED)**.  He criticized the BJP for using central enforcement agencies to target opposition figures while accusing the Congress of tacitly supporting these actions.  **Mr. Vijayan** asserted that the Communist movement would not be deterred and vowed to fight for democracy and equality, despite the damage caused to vehicles by protesting party workers who were subsequently arrested.

recent_articles.title: HDFC Bank shares fall 2% on reports of internal probe over Rs 45 cr interest payments - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **HDFC Bank** allegedly routed differential interest payments to the **Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC)**, a state government agency, through its marketing department disguised as road safety awareness campaign sponsorship. This practice violated RBI regulations and the bank's own anti-bribery policy. The bank’s former chairman, Atanu Chakraborty, resigned on March 18th citing ethical concerns related to these practices.  The bank's share prices have declined significantly since the resignation.

recent_articles.title: ED raids former Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan’s houses in CMRL pay-off case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Enforcement Directorate (ED)** conducted raids on the homes of former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his family, along with other locations across the state, in connection with an investigation into alleged political payoffs. The ED's action followed a High Court order allowing them to investigate **Exalogic**, a firm owned by Vijayan's daughter, T. Veena, which allegedly received monthly retainers from **Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL)** during the 2017-2021 period without providing tangible services. The ED is investigating whether these payments constituted money laundering.

recent_articles.title: Trump-backed Paxton topples Senator Cornyn in Texas primary run-off | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ken Paxton**, Texas Attorney General, defeated **John Cornyn** in the Republican primary run-off for US Senate, securing a November election that could decide control of the chamber.  Paxton's victory was fueled by President **Donald Trump's** endorsement and marked a significant blow to the party establishment. The outcome is likely to make Paxton the Democrats' top target in November as he faces off against Democratic state Representative **James Talarico**.

recent_articles.rephrased_article: Texas voters head to the polls for a runoff election in which Attorney General Ken Paxton faces incumbent Senator John Cornyn.  Trump endorsed Paxton, who is seeking to become the next US senator from Texas. recent_articles.title: Mundamveli residents lay day-long siege to GCDA headquarters - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Residents of the P&T Apartment Complex in Mundamveli protested at the **Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA)** headquarters on Tuesday, demanding a probe into alleged violations of distance norms from an 110 kV EHT line. The residents, who moved into the twin towers built by the GCDA in January 2024, have been facing electrical problems and leakage issues since moving in. **Kochi MLA Mohammed Shiyas** visited the protest site and promised to petition the Chief Minister for a Vigilance probe.  The GCDA maintains that the apartments were constructed with all necessary permissions but acknowledged the need to address the residents' concerns about the safety of the structures.

recent_articles.title: Australia politics live: Quad countries ink deal to build surveillance network and Fiji port to counter China | Australian politics | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A new report from the **National Tertiary Education Union (Nteu)** reveals that university class sizes have increased significantly since pre-pandemic levels, with over 27% of tutorials now exceeding 30 students.  The report found that just 9% of tutorials meet optimal standards for student support, leading to concerns about compromised workloads and declining student outcomes. **Dr Alison Barnes**, president of the Nteu, stated that this "class size explosion" is impacting universities nationwide. The Quad group of countries – Australia, the United States, India, and Japan – announced a new initiative to strengthen critical mineral supply chains and build surveillance capabilities in response to China's growing influence in the region.  The Quad also pledged to invest $20 billion in these initiatives and connect South Pacific islands through undersea cables by year-end.

recent_articles.title: Leader of Opposition R. Ashok criticises Congress government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **R. Ashok**, the **Opposition Leader in the Legislative Assembly**, criticized the **Congress party's** internal power struggle, stating that it has rendered the Karnataka government dysfunctional. He claimed that most ministers are in Delhi while the state administration lacks direction, and the high command is ineffective in restoring order.  **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, faces accusations of accumulating excessive debt through "unscientific and fiscally irresponsible guarantee schemes," according to **Ashok**.

recent_articles.title: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa mounts legal challenge against report that could lead to impeachment
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Cyril Ramaphosa**, South African president, has filed a legal challenge against a report that could lead to his impeachment. The report, commissioned by parliament, found potential misconduct related to the theft of cash from his private farm in 2020. **Ramaphosa** argues the panel misconstrued its mandate and misinterpreted the charges against him.  The report's findings paved the way for a parliamentary impeachment inquiry, which is now being led by a committee composed of MPs from various political parties.
